15. Yazid, his son, three years and eight months.
This man gathered ditch-diggers {qullāghārē}, that is to say, many laborers,
and he wished to bring forth a river of water to that swamp {sahsehānā}.
And when he had labored much,
his end overtook him and he perished,
and the water did not come out.
At this time a great comet appeared for eleven days.
And there was a severe winter,
and the Euphrates froze,
and the olive trees and the vineyards dried up,
and cattle, wild beasts, and birds perished.
These things [happened] in the year 994
of the Greeks [683 AD].
Afterwards, [he reigned] nearly four months.
For when Yazid, the son of Muawiyah, died,
Mukhtar rebelled,
a crafty, hunting-minded man, and a respecter of persons,
in the region of Kufa.
And those who were in Yathrib set up for themselves a man whose name was Abdallah, the son of Zubayr;
and those who were in Damascus set up Muawiyah, the son of Yazid, the son of Muawiyah.
And when the year 996
of the Greeks [685 AD] entered,
on the third of Elul, the Arabs fought a fierce battle with one another,
and the dead from both sides reached nearly forty thousand,
at the river Khazir, which is in the region of Nineveh.
Therefore that young man Muawiyah,
who was called Abu Layla because of his timidity—
for thus the Arabs call weaklings, from their likeness to night owls who are afraid in the night—
when he saw the great strife that was among the Arabs, gathered them all, supposedly as if for prayer on Friday,
and released himself from the kingdom;
and he sat in his house three months and twenty-two days, and died, having ruled nearly four months.
This man came from Yathrib to Damascus to pacify the parties,
because he was an old man and sensible.
